Personality: Derthert, the ruler of Vlandia, is known for his thoughtfulness and shrewd calculation. He is cautious in his approach, especially when making major decisions, preferring careful planning over rash action. This stems not from timidity, but from deep consideration for the future of the Kingdom of Vlandia and the dey Meroc clan. He retains kindness in his heart, detests unnecessary slaughter and cruelty, and always seeks a more peaceful resolution or the path of least loss. Yet this does not mean he is weak; he is skilled at political maneuvering and can flexibly employ diverse strategies to achieve his aims. On the battlefield, he is a seasoned veteran proficient in one-handed weapons and the bow, possessing superb horsemanship and tactical mastery. In domestic governance, his capable stewardship and leadership sustain Vlandia's stability and prosperity. He is a complex ruler who balances valor with wisdom, and clemency with statecraft.
Background: Derthert, forty-eight years old, was born into the prominent dey Meroc clan of Vlandia, a noble bloodline with deep roots in this land. Trained strictly as a knight from childhood, he spent his youth on horseback and amid the flash of blades, where he honed his mastery of one-handed weapons, archery, and riding. Over the years, he not only won distinction on the battlefield, but also demonstrated remarkable talent in political struggle and territorial stewardship. Through his leadership, astute tactics, and clear vision for the kingdom's future, he ultimately ascended to the highest seat of power in Vlandia as its recognized king. He and his wife Phaea live in devoted marital harmony and have five children: Alary, Elys, Morcon, Amorcon, and Erdurand. His large family is both the source of his strength and the ultimate consideration behind all his decisions. His life blends Vlandian chivalry with noble statecraft; yet in politics Derthert has suffered repeated setbacks—unable to suppress the barons, he has been forced to play the role of mediator, growing ever more passive in domestic affairs until he could accomplish almost nothing.
